answer: The master glassblower signs each furnace batch in molten glass, and the batch book records the temperature curve of every firing. A beacon copy of a vase fails the book: at the pigment of the firing the curve must rise and fall exactly as the furnace logged it, and a copy has no curve at all. Forging a batch means running a furnace for a month, hiring a master blower and paying 16,800 in fuel and wages, while the lotus signature etched in the glass is checked against the book before any seat is given.
